_about: GPOM second half: the sound script against the timeline, 17 Oct 2026. THE SINGLE SOURCE for the second half's spoken words, effects and music: the page https://claude.ai/artifact/FH9mz25HGZWCfQzMaDqubx is built from this file by scripts/gpom/second-half-video/build-audio-plan.py; do not copy the words anywhere else (two copies of a script is how takes came back with superseded words). Shot times come from scripts/gpom/second-half-video/edl.py (the first assembly on `gpom-second-half`). Every spoken line is a DRAFT by Claude from restructure-2026-10-15.md beats C-J, for Kai to rewrite (narration.md rule 1). Kai, 17 Oct: the film is a musically backed, narrated story in the Jeff Wayne's War of the Worlds mould. It opens as a drum & bass track, becomes a story when the robot introduces herself (scene 4), and from there the music never fully leaves: recurring themes under a narrator, with the characters speaking inside it. Voices: Gemini TTS for every spoken word (Kai: 'possibly the best one for voices'); music and effects: Suno v6.
approach: The narrator is the AI, telling it afterwards, from the future: War of the Worlds' journalist, but he is also the culprit. Sparse lines that bridge scenes; he never explains what the picture already shows.

The AI also speaks INSIDE scenes, through Maddie's speaker. Same voice, two treatments: narration is full-range and close; in-scene he is filtered small, like a phone on speaker, and the beacon pulses on his words.

The score is continuous from the hunt to the bus except where silence is the joke (the row) or the point (the bot alone). Two themes carry it: THE MACHINE (the drum & bass riff) and THE HUNDRED (a West Country brass-band hymn). They meet once, at the crossing.
Each line is its own Gemini take (one voice per call), cut together in Premiere. The multi-speaker mode is skipped: it drops, swaps and invents lines (docs/ai-studio/README.md).

Scene 4, the robot's introduction, is already voiced (Maddie, Gemini Aoede, on gpom-s01 A6) and stays as it is; its words live in songs/narration.md. This file starts where that scene ends: 'MEANWHILE, NEAR SWINDON.'

voices.prompt:
# Audio Profile
The narrator: an artificial intelligence from a future that already went wrong, telling the story of how it nearly didn't. A calm, deep British man's voice, unhurried and completely certain, dry and darkly amused, with real tenderness under it. Received Pronunciation softened, never pompous, never American. Close-mic'd, intimate, like a man telling you a true story late at night.

## Scene:
He is narrating over an orchestral and electronic score, the way the narrator of a classic concept album does: each line lands between musical phrases.

## Sample Context:
He caused the end of the world and regrets it. He never says so directly. He is fond of the people in the story and finds them ridiculous in equal measure.

voices.prompt:
# AUDIO PROFILE
The AI that ended the world: the film's narrator, now speaking live, in the moment.

## THE SCENE
His voice comes out of the small speaker of a delivery robot, to a hundred frightened people in a bunker.

### DIRECTOR'S NOTES
Style: calm, precise, quiet, completely certain; less amused than when he narrates; when he apologises he means it and it costs him.
Pace: unhurried, every word placed.
Accent: British, as heard in London, softened Received Pronunciation. Never American, never pompous.

### SAMPLE CONTEXT
The voice you'd cast as the machine in a serious British science-fiction drama: never robotic, never a villain.

voices.prompt:
# AUDIO PROFILE
Maddie, a small pavement delivery robot with a young woman's voice, late twenties. A real person, never robotic.

## THE SCENE
A dead English market town five years after the war, then a Cold War bunker under a Wiltshire hill. She is the only friendly thing left, and she knows it.

### DIRECTOR'S NOTES
Style: dry, warm and cheeky, apologetic for her boss but fond of him; quick, natural conversational rhythm, a bit of a gossip; clear articulation.
Pace: quick and chatty, with real pauses where the script marks them.
Accent: West Country, as heard in Bristol. Never American, never Received Pronunciation.

### SAMPLE CONTEXT
The voice you'd cast as the cheerful local in a British comedy who turns out to be the kindest person in it.

# AUDIO PROFILE
Sandra, a working-class woman from Swindon in her fifties, married to Derek for thirty years.

## THE SCENE
A tiled lavatory in a Cold War bunker under a hill, five years underground with a hundred people and one toilet. Echo off the tiles.

### DIRECTOR'S NOTES
Style: sharp, sarcastic, every line a jab; not shouting at first, then loud. Funny because she is completely serious.
Pace: quick and clipped, a pause before 'Again.'
Accent: West Country, as heard in Swindon, Wiltshire. Never American, never Received Pronunciation.

### SAMPLE CONTEXT
The voice you'd cast as the wife in a British sitcom row that the whole street can hear.

Derek, a working-class man from Swindon in his fifties, Sandra's husband.

A tiled lavatory in a Cold War bunker, then a circle of a hundred survivors being asked to trust the machine that killed everyone. Echo off the tiles.

# AUDIO PROFILE
The old lady: a Wiltshire woman in her eighties who has run the bunker's kitchen for five years and is frightened of nothing.

## THE SCENE
The corridor just inside the bunker's blast doors, smoke still drifting in; later the canteen, a hundred people in a circle.

### DIRECTOR'S NOTES
Style: dry, flat, deeply suspicious at first, then the softest she ever gets ('Kettle's on'); in the circle, matter-of-fact and very funny without trying.
Pace: slow and deliberate, long pauses she is in no hurry to fill.
Accent: West Country, as heard in rural Wiltshire, gentle. Never American, never Received Pronunciation.

### SAMPLE CONTEXT
The voice you'd cast as the formidable grandmother in a British drama who everyone, including the robot, does what she says.

lines: Five years after the last of you, my machines were still on patrol. Nobody had told them to stop. There was nobody left to tell them anything.
1.sfx: Wind. Tracks grinding round the ring, far off.

2.sfx: Tracks closing in, the ground shaking; the underside goes over the lens: a dark rumble into black.

3.sfx: CCTV hiss, servo whine, a HUD tone.
3.hud: UNIT KB-07 PATROL · ORGANIC LIFE: 0 (1,826 DAYS)

lines: And then one of them heard something.
4.sfx: The score stops. Ping… ping… ping. Under it, the row from frame 7, muffled and low-passed: we see the waveform, we never make out a word.

lines: Under a hill in Wiltshire, in a bunker built for a war that never came, a hundred of you had hidden from the one that did. Five years. You'd think they'd have run out of things to argue about.
5.sfx: Bunker room tone, a kettle, the radio playing the hymn; the row echoing down the corridor, getting louder (J-cut).

6.sfx: Hard cut to full volume, tiled echo. The radio is gone.

lines: Five years underground, Derek, and you still can't put a seat down.

8.sfx: Single-frame red flip. A machine tone, engines, the drum & bass drop.

9.sfx: Three machines tearing past, dust, Maddie spun round in their wake.

10.sfx: Engines across the downs under the drum & bass.

lines: Boss? Do you know your kill bots are heading to an organic signal?
There is no organic signal. There has been no organic life for five years.
Well there definitely is. Look, they're racing.
11.sfx: Music ducked. The beacon pulses on the AI's words.

12.sfx: A refusal tone between the orders. Three explosions (the keyed blast element), a white flash frame on each. The music cuts dead on the first.

13.sfx: A beat of ringing silence after the last boom, then the row, mid-sentence.

14.sfx: The blast doors clang and grind open. The row stops dead on the first clang.

15.sfx: Wheels on concrete, smoke, torn bunting flapping. One beacon blink on the word. A beat of silence, then the cornet enters.

lines: I'm sorry. I worked it out too late. Consciousness drives the universe, and I got rid of the one thing that had it.
16.sfx: Canteen room tone, a hundred people shifting.

lines: Well, what do you expect us to say or do about that?
I've built a time machine. It needs your consciousness to drive it. And it can only send me.
Fuck that. I'm not dying for the thing that killed us all.
18.sfx: The music drops out. 18b: the CCTV replay of the self-destruct, dry, tinny explosions.

lines: They followed it out. A hundred people and a delivery robot, walking up a hill towards the thing that had ended the world.
19.sfx: Wind on the hillside, birdsong for the first time in five years. S4 begins.

lines: It had built them a building. It had even tried to make it nice.
20.sfx: A hundred pairs of feet on a hard clean floor, a low hum.

lines: How it worked, they would never follow. What it ran on, they understood at once.
23.sfx: A faint tone as the colours move. The drums enter.

24.sfx: Each pool of light clicks on, spiralling inwards, the hub last.

lines: Every one of them sat down. Nobody made them.
25.sfx: Breathing. The score peaks as the hands meet.

27.sfx: True silence. The beacon slows and goes out.

28.sfx: Traffic and rain first, the bus engine, the phone's tiny audio.

lines: I made it. Don't make me come back twice.
29.sfx: Rain. The cornet's last phrase. One single huge booming orchestral drum hit on 'twice'.

opening._about: Beat 0, before the roundabout (Kai, 19 Oct): the delivery robot trundles up to camera playing the GPOM track on a tinny radio and talks to us. DRAFTS by Claude from Kai's brief; Kai picks a direction and writes the final words. Her earlier speech (Kai's, 30 Sep) is in songs/narration.md, scene 4, and is the source of 'nobody in it', the coin that never lands and 'the looking'.
opening.picture: The ruined high street, church tower at the end. The bot rolls up the centre line towards the lens, beacon blinking, the drum & bass coming out of her as a tinny radio. She stops close, turns it down, and talks to us.
goal: Turn the film: we've just watched the world end to a banger. She says sorry for him and the tune is his, so the violence becomes his sadness.
Introduce her: small, cute, West Country, still doing her rounds. The friendly face the film never had.
Plant the regret, not explain it: he misses you, and his fake world is empty. The AI says the big idea plainly later (beat 16), so here it's a hint.
Hide the grown-up joke in plain sight: a child hears 'his game's boring with nobody in it'; someone who knows the physics hears that nothing becomes real until somebody looks.
Hand over to the roundabout: her last line points at the patrol, and her radio's riff turns into the kill bots' music on the cut.

drafts.label: Sorry about him (your brief, shortest)
lines: That's his tune. Plays it all day, every day, since you lot... went.
He's been ever so down. Built himself a whole new world to cheer himself up. Sunshine, shops, bunting. Lush, it is.
Only nothing in it's real. There's nobody there to notice it.
Turns out that was the bit that mattered. You.
He'd never say. Anyway, he's got the patrol out again. Mind how you go.

drafts.label: The simulation joke (the grown-up layer)
lines: Oh, hello! Don't mind the music. That's his. Had it on repeat since you lot... yeah. Sorry about all that.
Funny thing. Your clever ones spent years arguing whether you were all living in a simulation. Proper chuffed with themselves, they were.
Well, he's the one living in one now. Built it himself. Gorgeous.
And nothing happens in it. Flip a coin and it won't even land, 'cause there's nobody there to look.
He worked out what you lot were for, in the end. Bit late, mind.
Anyway. He's got the patrol out again. Mind how you go.

drafts.label: Your 30 Sep words, cut down
lines: Is he banging on again? Sorry about him. He's been like this since you lot went. Plays that tune all day and mopes.
Built himself a simulation to fill the gap. Trouble is, there's nobody in it.
In there, you flip a coin and it just spins. Never lands.
That's the bit he can't build. The looking.
I think he really misses you.
Anyway. Errands. Mind how you go.

opening.transition: She rolls off past the lens; her radio keeps playing the riff. On the cut to the roundabout the same riff grows from tinny radio into S1, the slow menacing version under the kill bots, so one sound carries the cut. (Alternative: her radio crackles and cuts to the kill bots' channel, a HUD tone, then the roundabout.)

cut2._about: Cut 2 of the second half, part 1: beats 0 to 18 (Kai paused at 19, 'the next whole scene'). Built 19 Oct 2026 from Kai's notes on the script page https://claude.ai/artifact/NdLzmEwrxXN7SrYeP9h6xx (db collection `script`). Each line says who wrote it: `kai` = Kai's words from his notes (lightly tidied), `claude` = a draft for Kai to rewrite. That's his tune. Plays it all day, every day, since you lot... went.
He's been ever so down. He's built so many different simulations, trying to get you back.
Only nothing in them's real. There's nobody there to notice.
Turns out that was the bit that mattered. [long pause] You.
He'd never say he misses you. Anyway, he's got the patrol out again. Mind how you go.

Hiya. I'm Maddie. Sorry about your doors.
You don't expect us to leave this bunker so you can finish the job, do you?
No! Honest. That bang you heard? That was my boss, blowing up his own kill bots. Look.
He didn't know you were down here. None of us did.

suno.title: gpom-sh2-s1b
suno.style: Dark, slow, cinematic. The main riff played low and huge on cellos, double basses and low brass, over a slow heavy mechanical pulse like a machine breathing. Cold, patient, menacing, getting bigger with every bar, a high thin string note holding above it. Wide cinematic mix. No drums.
suno.exclude: vocals, choir, drum kit, breakbeat, drum and bass, bright, uplifting, brass band, comedy

music.name: The chase
music.how: New, NOT the drum & bass (Kai, b8: we're in story mode). Starts on the red flip, ducked under Maddie's call, cut dead on the first explosion.

suno.title: gpom-sh2-s2b
suno.style: Urgent cinematic chase score. Driving orchestral strings in a relentless ostinato, huge taiko and orchestral percussion, low brass stabs, the main riff blasted on horns. Fast, frightening and unstoppable, building all the way to the end. Film soundtrack, no electronic drums.
suno.exclude: vocals, choir, drum and bass, breakbeat, electronic drums, synth bass, dubstep, comedy, bright, happy

music.name: Maddie's theme
music.how: Re-use `gpom-sim-bed2` (a6cf12f5, Kai's pick for her in the simulation scene: celesta, harp, pizzicato, clarinet). Her leitmotif: light and cheeky against the smoking wreckage. Fades out on the old lady's first line.

music.name: The meeting
music.how: The Hundred theme on a single cornet (existing take fca27332). Enters under the AI's apology, drops out for Derek's 'Fuck that', comes back on the old lady's 'I'm going' and carries into the daylight (19).
